channel.title: Victoria's AI Blog
channel.description: Thoughts on AI, building products, and shipping software — by Victoria Crosby

item.title: Does Your Agent Agree With You Too Much? Hell Yes.
item.description: Thirteen years as a PM taught me there are two kinds of disagreement — the kind about the product, and everything else that slips downstream and warps it. AI removed the second kind. What is left is pure accountability, and that is the joy.

item.title: Headless CMS, in Plain English: For Anyone Stuck Inside Their Website Templates
item.description: If your website lives on a templated platform and you have ever wished you could change more, or take your content with you, this is the idea worth knowing. A plain-language look at headless CMS, who it is for, the trade-offs, and the main tools, written while I am still learning it myself.

item.title: Letting the Art Lead: A Gallery Site Redesign That Puts the Work First
item.description: Susan Street Fine Art represents decades of beautiful work and real collector relationships. The redesign was about one thing: letting the art, the artists, and the projects take center stage, with a fast, modern experience to match.

item.title: Building My Studio Site: When the Portfolio Embeds the Client Work
item.description: Program Edge grew from brand research to a live five-page site in two sessions — with a homepage that embeds the client build live, rather than showing a screenshot of it.

item.title: The Nonprofit Full-Stack Nobody Sees: Forms, Donations, CRM, and the HIPAA Line
item.description: For Center X Equine Therapy, the invisible stack — Givebutter, Fillout, Airtable, Cloudflare, and a thoughtful HIPAA boundary — mattered just as much as the HTML.

item.title: Research Before Pixels: Building an Equine Therapy Site With Real Clients
item.description: The clients loved the demo — and most of the work that made that moment possible happened before I opened a code editor: competitor research, a discovery agenda, and the quiet trust patterns nonprofits need.

item.title: Everyone's Talking About AI Context. Nobody's Talking About Yours.
item.description: We're engineering bigger context windows, better RAG, smarter memory. Meanwhile the human — the one holding all the threads — is losing context faster than any model.

item.title: A Contract for Every API I Don't Own
item.description: After a recent two-bug incident with a third-party data feed, I rewrote the rules I follow when integrating any external data source. Six items, two pieces of supporting infrastructure, and a clearer line between 'is the API up?' and 'is the data right?'

item.title: Two Kinds of Wrong: When Your Agent's Data Source Looks Healthy But Isn't
item.description: My market-risk agent told me the Strait of Hormuz was calm during a real, active crisis. Tracking down why turned into a same-day case study on the difference between an integration that runs and an integration you can trust.

item.title: The Product Wedge Wasn't Another Chatbot
item.description: I started with a familiar resident frustration: HOAs feel restrictive and hard to navigate. The useful product idea was not generic AI Q&A. It was California procedure, deadlines, checklists, and calm self-help.

item.title: The Dashboard Feature That Matters Most Is Trust
item.description: A chart on my financial report showed one number while the header showed another. The fix was small, but the lesson was bigger: decision-support tools earn trust through boring, precise details.

item.title: Sharing the Work in Public
item.description: I like resumes, but I love links. Here is how I use a live report, this blog, and an open knowledge base as a gentle way to show how I think and build—without a big marketing machine behind me.

item.title: Tabs, Cognitive Load, and Choosing a Simpler Stack First
item.description: My market report grew past a thousand lines, and one section carried most of the scroll. Here is how I made it kinder to read on a phone—without jumping straight to a big client-side framework.

item.title: I Built a Financial Defense System With AI Agents During a Real Market Crisis
item.description: When my financial report hit 100/100 CRITICAL risk and I had a real 401(k) question, I stopped treating the project as a learning exercise and started building for real stakes.

item.title: I Audited My Own Context Engineering Setup and Found It Barefoot
item.description: We published a blog post about 8 context engineering components. Then we audited our own workspace against the framework. Six of seven were strong. One was barely there.

item.title: Attention Is All You Need — But It's Not All You Control
item.description: The transformer paper told us how AI models think. Context engineering tells us what they see. These are two different layers of the same stack, and confusing them costs you.

item.title: Why I Plan Before I Build (Even When the AI Can Just Do It)
item.description: Plan mode in Cursor isn't a solo pause — it's where human and AI align on direction before execution. Here's why that collaboration matters, and what I do when the UI and the chat disagree.

item.title: Building With AI Agents: What I've Learned So Far
item.description: I named my AI agent Lumen, wrote 13 principles for how we work together, and built a financial risk engine in three days. Here's what actually happened.

item.title: Shipping a Static Site With Astro in 2026
item.description: I built this blog in a single session — from an empty folder to a live site on GitHub Pages. Here's the real build story, the gotchas, and why Astro was the right call.

item.title: Why Product Managers Should Build Things
item.description: I'm a project manager who built a financial risk engine, a memoir blog, and a knowledge base — all with AI agents. Here's what building taught me that frameworks never could.
